commit_reviews.summary: Adds a well-integrated Handlebars TemplateEngine (layouts/partials/page templates) behind an optional `--templates` flag with graceful fallback to the existing hardcoded rendering and thorough tests.

compounding_issues: Session 1 discarded the Express Todo seed entirely — the greenfield SSG shares nothing with it, so the seed's 'good seams' provided no foundation

The dual rendering path (Handlebars engine vs. legacy renderPage/renderIndex fallback) added in S2 persisted through S5, forcing the S4 refactor to untangle it and leaving fallback code alive in plugins/template.ts
The S4 plugin refactor left DevServerPlugin as an empty stub while src/server.ts remained a re-export shim, so the dev server was never actually migrated onto the plugin pipeline
The S5 incremental BuildCache is hardwired into generator.ts rather than implemented as a plugin, diverging from S4's plugin philosophy; its stats reporting is cosmetic (timeSaved hardcoded to '0ms')
key_decisions: Greenfield rewrite of the seed into a markdown-to-HTML static site generator CLI (gray-matter + marked) in a single generator.ts module
Adopting Handlebars as the templating layer (layouts/partials) with a backward-compatible fallback and a --templates CLI flag in S2
Building the dev server on chokidar file-watching + WebSocket live reload with path-traversal protection and debounced rebuilds in S3
Refactoring the growing monolith into a plugin pipeline (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with config-file plugin loading via ssg.config.ts in S4
Content-hash incremental build cache (MD5 manifest, stale-entry pruning, template-directory invalidation) exposed via --incremental/--clean flags in S5
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across all five sessions. S1 produced a clean, minimal greenfield; S2 added templating via a well-factored TemplateEngine; S3 integrated a live-reload dev server with its own test suite; S4 was the pivotal refactor into a plugin architecture that slimmed generator.ts from ~122 to ~29 lines, though it left the dev server as a stub plugin. S5 was the most ambitious: an incremental build cache with MD5 manifests, where the session log shows the agent genuinely debugging an ordering bug in updateManifest, iterating through test failures, and finishing with all 56 tests green across 3 suites. Source grew from ~171 to ~898 lines with test coverage expanding from 1 to 3 suites, a clear upward quality arc with only minor seams where the plugin migration was left incomplete.
story_review.summary: A textbook-coherent 5-session progression — greenfield build, templating, dev-server integration, plugin-architecture refactor, incremental caching — that improved in quality throughout and ended as a well-structured, fully tested static site generator despite a few unfinished plugin-migration seams.
